title: Sermones Sancto Ambrosio Hactenus Ascripti
author: Ambrose

passages.original: Primum itaque hoc considerare debemus, quod non est acceptor Dominus personarum (est enim aequus judex et justus) sed pro K qualitate morum rependat dilectionis affectum : et eum eligat non qui verbis promptus, devotione piger, sed qui fuerit lingua tacitus, meniedevotus, de quo dicit Propheta : Tacitum te faciens, sapiens videberis (Prov. XVII, 28). De illo autem qui petulanter loquitur , refert Scriptura : Non omnis qui dicit mihi, Domine, Domine, intrabit in regnum cœlorum : sed qui fecerit voluntatem meam (Matth.
passages.english: So the first thing we ought to consider is this: the Lord is no respecter of persons (for he is a fair and just judge), but he repays the affection of his love according to the quality of [our] conduct; and he chooses not the one who is ready with words but sluggish in devotion, but the one who is silent in tongue and devout in mind, of whom the Prophet says: "By keeping yourself silent you will be thought wise" (Prov. 17:28). But of the one who speaks impudently Scripture reports: "Not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does my will" (Matt.
passages.notes: The stray "K" before "qualitate" is taken as a printer's mark and omitted. "meniedevotus" is read as "mente devotus" (devout in mind). The quotation attributed to "the Prophet" is from Proverbs. The biblical reference is completed in the following context (7:21).

passages.original: Habemus apud Maximum alium sermonem de eodem sancto in multis huic ipsi persimilem, sed sive illi ab eodem auctore, sive a diversi, profecti fuerint, hunc non esse Maximi perspicuum est ; cum in ipsamet Vercellensi Ecclesiasit pronuntiatus. Ejus vero auctorem antiquum fuisseex eo patet, quod re, præsente Exsuperantio. ejusdem Eusebii discipulo, loqui significat. Verum quisquis ille sit, diversum eum esse ab Ambrosio, et alii jam ante agnoverunt, et tota sermonis series abunde probat.
passages.english: We have in Maximus another sermon on the same saint, very similar to this one in many respects. But whether they came from the same author or from different ones, it is clear that this one is not by Maximus, since it was delivered in the very Church of Vercelli. That its author was ancient is evident from the fact that he indicates he is speaking in the presence of Exsuperantius, a disciple of that same Eusebius. But whoever he may be, others have already recognised before now that he is different from Ambrose, and the whole course of the sermon amply proves it.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: "diversi" read as "diversis", "Ecclesiasit" as "Ecclesia sit", "fuisseex" as "fuisse ex". The phrase "quod re, præsente" seems corrupt, perhaps for "quod se, præsente"; translated as "that he indicates he is speaking in the presence of".
